title: Causal Discovery beyond Conditional Independence: Identifiability, Algorithms, and Statistical Inference for Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2610.23543v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Learning causal structure from data requires assumptions about mechanisms, noises, observation schemes, and interventions. Historically, causal discovery has relied primarily on conditional independence. This review focuses on modern causal discovery methods that exploit properties of distributions beyond conditional independence. Our organizing principle separates the source of identification from the statistical estimator and its computational implementation. This perspective connects conditional-independence methods with distributional asymmetries, conditional-moment restrictions, and variation across environments or individuals. We examine discovery under latent confounding and feedback, distinguishing causal information about observed variables from reconstruction of latent structure and emphasizing the additional semantics required by cyclic models. translated_title: 超越条件独立的因果发现：有向无环图与循环图的可识别性、算法与统计推断
translated_abstract: 从数据中学习因果结构需要对机制、噪声、观测方案和干预做出假设。历史上，因果发现主要依赖条件独立性。本综述聚焦于利用条件独立性之外的分布性质的现代因果发现方法。我们的组织原则是将识别来源与统计估计量及其计算实现分离开来。这一视角将条件独立方法与分布不对称性、条件矩约束以及跨环境或跨个体的变异联系起来。我们考察了存在潜在混淆与反馈情况下的因果发现，区分了关于观测变量的因果信息与潜在结构的重构，并强调了循环模型所需的额外语义。我们还区分了总体层面的可识别性与频率学派及贝叶斯一致性（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 本综述系统梳理了超越条件独立性的现代因果发现方法，提出将识别来源与统计估计相分离的统一框架，涵盖分布不对称、条件矩约束和跨环境变异等手段，并讨论了潜在混淆与循环图下的可识别性、算法与统计推断。
en_tdlr: This review surveys modern causal discovery methods beyond conditional independence, unifying identification sources—distributional asymmetries, conditional moment restrictions, and cross-environment variation—with estimators and inference for both DAG and cyclic models under latent confounding and feedback.
